Expected utility sum_k p_k r_k(p_k) with unknown Lipschitz r_k: [0,1] -> [0,1] (known Lipschitz constants L_k in (0,1])

algorithms.name: Standard bandit algorithm (e.g. UCB1) on uniformly discretized meta-arm space

conditions: r_k Lipschitz with known constant L_k in (0,1]

source.label: theorem:key_theorem_vanilla
source.quote: Let $\epsilon=\Theta\big((\ln T/T)^{1/3}\big)$. The regret of Algorithm \ref{algo:action_UCB} (with respect to the optimal arm in non-discretized $\cP$) is upper bounded as follows: $\reg(T) = \cO\big(KT^{2/3}(\ln T)^{1/3}\big)$.

results.notes: Regret defined via expected utilities against best fixed meta arm, so pseudo-regret. Algorithm maximizes UCB over exponentially many meta arms; compute not stated. Remark D.6 states O~(K^{4/3}T^{2/3}) when only one arm is activated per round.

conditions: base algorithm achieves O(sqrt(|P_eps| T ln T)) regret on the finite discretized set

source.label: lemma:regret_bound_naive
source.quote: Let $\epsilon = \Theta \big(\big(\frac{\ln T}{T }\big)^\frac{1}{K+1}\big)$. Running a bandit algorithm which achieves optimal regret $\cO(\sqrt{|\cP_\epsilon|T\ln T})$ on the strategy space $\cP_\epsilon$ attains the following regret (w.r.t. the optimal arm in non-discretized $\cP$): $\reg(T) = \cO\big(T^{\frac{K}{K+1}}{(\ln T)}^{\frac{1}{K+1}}\big)$.

results.notes: Naive baseline; proof gives a K-dependent constant c = Theta(K (L*)^{(K-1)/(K+1)}) hidden in O.

symbols.rho: ratio of estimation-stage rounds to phase length, constant in (0,1)
symbols.gamma: time-discount factor of the impact function

source.label: theorem: key_theorem_neq_1
source.quote: For any constant ratio $\rho\in(0,1)$ and $\gamma\in(0,1)$, let $\epsilon= \Theta((\ln(T\rho)/(T\rho))^{1/3})$ and $s_a= \Theta(\ln(\epsilon^{1/3}/K)/\ln\gamma)$. The regret of Algorithm \ref{algo:reduction_algo} with Algorithm \ref{algo:history-dependent} as input bounds as follows: $\reg(T) = \cO\big( K T^{2/3}\left((\ln (T\rho))/\rho\right)^{1/3}\big)$.

results.notes: Algorithm needs gamma to set s_a (not in vocabulary). Comparator is the best fixed meta arm.

source.label: theorem_low_bound_all
source.quote: Let $T > 2K$ and $K \geq 4$, there exist problem instances that for our action- and history-dependent bandits, respectively, the regret for any algorithm $\cA$ follows: $\inf_{\cA} \reg(T) \geq \Omega(K T^{2/3})$.

results.notes: Action-dependent part; restated as Theorem F.2. Hard instances use Bernoulli rewards with Lipschitz bump functions (L_k = 1).

conditions: reward functions satisfy the strictly proper utility property

source.label: theorem_low_bound_all
source.quote: Let $T > 2K$ and $K \geq 4$, there exist problem instances that for our action- and history-dependent bandits, respectively, the regret for any algorithm $\cA$ follows: $\inf_{\cA} \reg(T) \geq \Omega(K T^{2/3})$.

results.notes: History-dependent part, proved by reduction to action-dependent lower bound in Appendix G.

conditions: algorithm is Thompson Sampling (Beta-Bernoulli) that ignores the action impact, treating sample means as true means

source.label: lem:TS_fail
source.quote: For the reward structure defined in Example \ref{exmpl_2}, Thompson Sampling would suffer linear regret if it doesn't consider the action's impact it deploys at every time round, namely, it takes the sample mean as the true mean reward of each arm.

results.notes: Negative result; Lemma C.5 gives the same for mean-converging algorithms (incl. UCB). Linear regret recorded as Omega(T).
